key_insight: Generative (decoder-based) LLMs can be used as semantics-aware evaluators for ASR: they reliably pick better hypotheses and produce meaning-driven distances/labels that complement or improve upon WER and embedding-only metrics.
problem_solved: WER is insensitive to meaning and can mislead ASR assessment; the paper addresses the need for evaluation metrics that reflect semantic fidelity and human perception.
method: Pairwise selection: use a generative LLM to choose the better transcription from two ASR hypotheses.
Generative embeddings / semantic distance: extract LLM-derived embeddings or similarity scores to compute meaning-based distance between reference and hypothesis.

Qualitative classification/analysis: prompt the LLM to produce human-readable error categories or qualitative judgments to explain semantic failures; compare these signals to WER and embedding-based metrics.
impact: Provides practical, semantics-aware evaluation tools that align ASR scoring with human judgment, helping researchers and engineers prioritize real-world errors and improve model development/benchmarking.
visual_elements: Three-panel flowchart showing the three approaches (pairwise selection, semantic-distance via embeddings, qualitative classification) from audio → ASR hypotheses → LLM evaluator → score/label.
Bar chart or scatter plot comparing correlation of WER, embedding-based metrics, and LLM-based scores with human judgments.
Example pairwise comparison card (audio waveform + two transcriptions) showing the LLM's chosen preferred hypothesis and short rationale.
Embedding-space visualization (t-SNE/UMAP) or heatmap illustrating semantic distances between references and hypotheses using LLM embeddings.
paper_title: Evaluation of Automatic Speech Recognition Using Generative Large Language Models
paper_authors: Thibault Bañeras-Roux, Shashi Kumar, Driss Khalil, Sergio Burdisso, Petr Motlicek
